title: VTP Pruning
description: Enable VTP pruning to stop unnecessary VLAN traffic being sent for VLANs absent on the far switch.
scenario: Enable VTP pruning to stop unnecessary VLAN traffic being sent for VLANs absent on the far switch.

concepts.title: What is VTP Pruning?
concepts.body: VTP Pruning restricts traffic for VLANs on a trunk that are not present on the other end. If a VLAN has no ports on the neighboring switch, the VTP server does not forward it.
concepts.code:
Before: SW1 sends all VLANs over trunk
After:  VTP pruning skips unused VLANs

concepts.title: How VTP Pruning Works
concepts.body: The VTP server maintains a "prune-eligible" list. Note it is only effective when VTP is in Server mode.
concepts.code:
Prune list → VLANs not to forward
Pruning applies only in VTP Server mode

concepts.title: Enabling VTP Pruning
concepts.body: Enable globally with "vtp pruning". Verify with "show vtp status" showing "VTP Pruning Mode: Enabled".
concepts.code:
SW1(config)# vtp pruning
SW1# show vtp status
VTP Pruning Mode: Enabled

concepts.title: Pruning vs Allowed VLANs
concepts.body: VTP pruning is automatic per-VLAN. "switchport trunk allowed vlan" is manual. Both reduce unnecessary trunk traffic.
concepts.code:
VTP pruning: dynamic/global
Allowed VLANs: per-trunk/manual
